themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints skyrocketed to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 1500% spike—suggesting a specific new disturbance or event may be occurring in Upper West Side parks that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 6 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.08)
1500% increase from 8-week average, statistically significant anomaly
No Reddit discussion or local news coverage yet suggests underreported issue
reporting_angles: What specific park venue or event triggered the sudden noise complaints—construction, concerts, sports leagues, or gatherings?
Interview residents near affected parks and Parks Department to identify the source and timeline

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints hit 10 this week, triple the 3.1 weekly average—a 220% spike—indicating a possible shift in street-level activity or enforcement that aligns with the community board's long-standing request for expanded street outreach.
evidence: 10 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.42)
220% increase signals new pattern not explained by seasonal variation
Community board has repeatedly requested expanded street outreach, suggesting underlying unmet demand
reporting_angles: Are specific subway stations or commercial corridors experiencing increased panhandling, and if so, why now?
Interview NYPD, outreach workers, and affected businesses to understand whether this reflects increased homelessness, enforcement changes, or displacement from other areas

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 6 this week from a baseline of 1.2 per week—a 380% increase (z-score: 4.91)—suggesting coordinated or opportunistic damage to the neighborhood's urban forest in the past few days.
evidence: 6 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.91)
380% spike suggests clustering rather than random incidents
Community board has standing request for park/amenity reconstruction, indicating environmental maintenance is a district priority
reporting_angles: Map the locations of this week's 6 complaints to identify if damage is concentrated in specific parks or corridors (e.g., Central Park edges, side streets)
Interview Parks Department and residents to determine if damage is weather-related, contractor activity, or deliberate vandalism

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining-related complaints spiked to 11 last week from a baseline of 1.8 per week—a 529% increase—likely reflecting implementation of new dining sheds, permit violations, or maintenance issues affecting sidewalk access in the past 7-10 days.
evidence: 11 outdoor dining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.27)
529% increase indicates sudden change in conditions or enforcement
High volume of 1108 DOB alterations filed in last 90 days may include dining shed installations
reporting_angles: Identify which outdoor dining establishments received new permits or expanded seating in the past two weeks
Interview community members and restaurant operators about specific complaints: blocked sidewalks, noise, sanitation, or ADA access issues

themes_detail.label: Building Code Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: SPIT (Special Projects Inspection Team) complaints reached 9 last week versus a baseline of 2.2—a 300% increase (z-score: 3.94)—paired with 1108 DOB alteration filings in 90 days, suggesting intensive code enforcement or widespread building violations across the district.
evidence: 9 SPIT complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.94)
300% spike coincides with 1108 DOB alteration filings over 90 days (1022 alterations alone)
Community board has standing request for expanded code enforcement, indicating chronic enforcement shortfall
reporting_angles: Which building types are triggering SPIT inspections—residential, commercial, or mixed-use—and what violations are most common?
Interview DOB and community board to assess whether spike reflects increased violations, improved complaint reporting, or targeted enforcement campaign
